headline: product-catalog's GetProduct fault (open incident inc-001) cannot be called recovered — it was still failing with zero successes at 10:00 UTC, and has since become unobservable because the load generator was deliberately paused. Do not read the last ~1h50m of silence as recovery: the errors stopped because the traffic stopped. The flag currently reads 'off', but exactly one request has reached the service in two hours, so nothing has actually re-tested it. High confidence.
severity_reasoning: Argued from user impact, and the honest answer has two halves. Right now the user impact is zero — not because the fault was fixed, but because there are no users at all: loadGeneratorTraffic is off and the only users in this environment are synthetic. Nobody is being stopped from buying anything at this moment, which is what rules out critical or high; I reserve those for active harm to someone trying to use the system, and there is nobody to harm. But this is not low either. The last direct observation of this code path, the 10:00 UTC bucket, shows 34.4 GetProduct errors against 0.0 successes — a total failure of the call, not a tapering one. GetProduct hydrates product detail pages, cart, recommendations and checkout, so if traffic resumes with the fault still armed this returns immediately to the sev2 blast radius already documented on inc-001 (~47% of checkout attempts failing). The thing actually at stake here is a decision, not a symptom: the next capability sees ~1h50m of zero product-catalog errors and the natural reading of that is 'recovered, close it'. That reading would close an unfixed sev2 on the revenue path. Medium reflects a real and consequential finding with no present victim.
hypothesis: The productCatalogFailure fault behind inc-001 was still active as recently as ~10:00-10:10 UTC. It did not taper out; the synthetic traffic that made it visible was switched off at ~10:10 UTC (and largely from ~08:46, with brief resumptions at 09:16-09:35 and 09:50-10:10). Since then product-catalog has received approximately one request in two hours — far too little to exercise the fault regardless of what governs it. The apparent quiet is therefore a measurement artifact of the paused load generator, not an observed change in the service's health. On the flag itself I am splitting two claims that I initially ran together: the CURRENT reading is 'off' and is probably accurate, since /toggle is the wrapper's only mutation route and /status reports the field it writes. What I cannot establish is the state during the symptom window — the same endpoint read 'off' at ~08:56 and 164.9 GetProduct errors followed it, and the wrapper serves no history. So the correct disposition is not 'the fault is still armed' and not 'the fault is fixed', but 'the fix has not been demonstrated, because nothing has exercised the path since it last failed'.
disconfirming_checks: Tried to explain the whole shift as a real outage first: the biggest signal was that checkout, payment, currency, shipping, email, quote and product-catalog all emitted ZERO spans in 60m. Ruled this out as a fault — flagd GET /status/loadGeneratorTraffic returns defaultVariant 'off' with description 'Turn off to pause all load-generator scenarios', and the load-generator's own logs say so verbatim in 200 of 200 lines sampled over the last 20m: 'Feature flag loadGeneratorTraffic evaluated to 0'. The generator is alive and polling, not crashed. A deliberately paused load generator is not an incident.

Ruled out the residual traffic being real users that could still exercise the fault: the flat residual (ad 31, cart 20, frontend 20 per 5m, unchanged for two hours) resolves entirely to ad 'GET /metrics' 180, image-provider 'GET /status' 538, frontend 'GET /' 60, cart 'POST' + flagd 'ResolveBoolean' 60, load-generator 'feature_flag.evaluate' 1968 over 30m. Scrapes, health checks and flag polls — no user-facing route anywhere. So no meaningful traffic is reaching GetProduct to test it.

Ruled out the competing error signals as unrelated background rather than folding them into this alert: ad and recommendation STATUS_CODE_ERROR is entirely span_name 'flagd.evaluation.v2.Service/EventStream', flat at ~1.1 per 10m (ad) and 1 per 20m (recommendation) in EVERY bucket from 07:57 to 11:57 — identical while the system was healthy and busy as while it is idle. Per my own investigation-heuristics playbook, errors against a flat error-rate metric are background. recommendation's headline '100% error rate' is a collapsed denominator (6 background errors / 6 total calls), not a regression.

Ruled out that I was blind rather than the system being quiet — the check that has to pass before any silence can be trusted: over 60m otelcol receiver_refused_spans=0, receiver_failed_spans=0, receiver_refused_log_records=0, receiver_failed_metric_points=0; accepted_spans=15683 vs exporter_sent_spans=31367 (2x fan-out); exporter_queue_size=0 of capacity 1000. The only Loki error lines in 45m are 3x otelcol-contrib 'Error scraping metrics' with scraper='process', at 7.1 errored of 44670 scraped points (0.016%), every other scraper at 0 — host process metrics, not the demo's telemetry. The zeros are real absence, not dropped data.

Argued the opposite case as hard as I could — that inc-001 HAS recovered — and it does not hold. The entire evidence for recovery is one request: Tempo returns exactly 1 product-catalog trace in 2h (cb6597b2a92829a2629d1561dc066d77 at 11:02:03 UTC), and it succeeded (rpc.response.status_code 'OK', reached the astronomy-db child span). But inc-001's own verified RCA established the fault is evaluated per product_id, and the prior shift observed failures across all ten product IDs; one success on product 0PUK6V6EV0 says nothing about the other nine. n=1 against a per-product fault is not evidence.

Ruled out treating the flag endpoint's 'off' as an all-clear — and I want the audit trail on this one, because I got it wrong in the middle. flagd GET /status/productCatalogFailure returns defaultVariant 'off' now and returned 'off' at ~08:56 during the prior shift. I first said targeting rules override that default; an independent challenge asserted the opposite (that /toggle writes defaultVariant, so it IS the armed state), and I retracted. That retraction was wrong: I had accepted a confident assertion without checking it. Checking it directly settles the matter — src/flagd/demo.flagd.json shows productCatalogFailure is the ONLY flag in the entire config carrying a 'targeting' block, and it keys on {"var":"product_id"} == "OLJCESPC7Z", which flagd evaluates ahead of defaultVariant. The wrapper's /status and /list return only defaultVariant and description and never surface 'targeting' at all. So the endpoint structurally cannot tell me whether this particular fault is armed. Corroborating timing evidence: sum(increase(...{span_name="oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[3h])) at 12:00 UTC = 164.9 errors occurring AFTER the 08:56 'off' reading, and the wrapper serves no history (/history, /events, /changes, /log, /audit all 404) while this project is read-only on flag state, so I cannot probe by toggling either.

Ruled out the one surviving successful request as evidence of recovery on a second, stronger ground than sample size. The fault targets product_id 'OLJCESPC7Z'. The single GetProduct that succeeded at 11:02:03 UTC was for demo.product.id '0PUK6V6EV0' ('Solar System Color Imager') — a different product, which the targeting rule does not cover. That request therefore could not have exercised the fault no matter what state the flag was in. It is not weak evidence of recovery; it is no evidence at all.

Checked whether a timestamped record of past flag evaluations exists that would settle the armed-state question outright, rather than settling for 'unknown' too early. feature_flag_evaluation_success_total does exist in Mimir with feature_flag_key / feature_flag_result_variant / feature_flag_result_reason labels — but over 6h it carries only four series, all job='opentelemetry-demo/cart' (failedReadinessProbe off=720/on=0, cartFailure off=444/100%=0). There is no product-catalog series, so this promising source has no coverage for the flag I care about. Worth noting it did confirm cart's own fault never fired (cartFailure variant='100%' count 0 over 6h).

Checked that I am not simply re-raising the carried-forward incident with no new information. inc-001's headline states 'most recent burst 08:50 UTC, quiet since'. The metric range contradicts that: GetProduct errored again at 09:30 (105.6 errors) and at 10:00 (34.4 errors against 0.0 successes). The incident's own timeline is stale, so this is new evidence, not a duplicate.
